title: Graceful rejoin checkpoint and load trim hotfix
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize regional rejoin path and trim aggressive tenant load spikes. Includes telemetry snapshots to prevent stale circuit reopen, improved per-tenant load-trim algorithm to avoid cascading evictions, and a regression test suite for checkpointed rejoin flows.
description: Context: Following a recent incident where large KV-drain replays caused long tail rejoin latencies and churn in regional circuits, this PR introduces a defensive hotfix that checkpoints lightweight node state at controlled quiesce points and applies an immediate load-trim for tenants that exceed burst budgets during failover. Motivation: reduce rejoin latency variance, prevent cascading tenant evictions during regional failover, and ensure SLO enforcement does not oscillate when nodes rejoin. High level changes: 1) rejoin checkpointing: add a compact snapshot (RejoinCheckpoint) recording tenant lease snapshots, KV-cache progress markers, and inflight request counts; checkpoints are written atomically to a local ephemeral store and garbage-collected after successful join. 2) load-trim algorithm: introduce TenantBurstTrim that computes a per-tenant trim factor from SLO credits and recent token burn rate; trims are bounded and applied as a conservative soft-shed (prefer prefix/kv-cache reuse) to avoid full eviction. 3) circuit latch unwind safety: telemetry snapshot reconciler detects stale OPEN->HALF_OPEN oscillations and enforces a minimum cooldown aligned with observed heartbeat windows. 4) small API surface: new metrics and traces (rejoin.checkpoint.duration, tenant.trim.factor, circuit.latch.cooldown) and a new CLI opt --skip-checkpoint for testing. Why this is a hotfix: behavior prevents immediate customer-visible regression by smoothing rejoin path; design is intentionally conservative and feature-flagged for gradual rollout. Checklist: [x] unit tests added for checkpoint serialization and GC [x] integration test for a simulated regional failover scenario [x] canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic burst profile [x] added telemetry dashboards and alerts for new metrics [x] documented opt-in runtime flag in ops runbook. Commits summary: - 6f3b2c1 Add RejoinCheckpoint model and lightweight local store - 9b2a7f8 Implement TenantBurstTrim and integrate with scheduler admission - d2a9f4e Circuit latch snapshot reconciler and cooldown enforcement - e7c1d0b Telemetry: metrics, traces, dashboards and alerts - f0a8c3a Tests: unit + integration harness and canary scripts. Files changed (high level): src/scheduler/rejoin_checkpoint.go, src/scheduler/checkpoint_store.go, src/slo/tenant_trim.go, src/circuit/latch_reconciler.go, internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go, cli/ops_flags.go, tests/integration/failover_rejoin_test.go, tests/e2e/canary_burst_profile.sh, docs/ops/rejoin_runbook.md, manifests/featureflags.yaml. Testing and canary: local unit and integration runs passed. Canary deployment to a small slice in us-west-2 ran for 2h with synthetic 3x token bursts; observed 45% reduction in 95th-percentile rejoin latency and no tenant eviction spikes. CI summary: build passed, unit tests passed, integration tests passed (one flaky e2e test retried and passed), lint passed, security-scan passed. Review conversation (high level): Reviewer Arjun asked for bounds on trim factor to avoid starving steady tenants; reply: implemented upper/lower bounds and added unit tests. Reviewer Diego requested telemetry labels include tenant_id hashing to avoid PII; reply: done, we emit tenant.hash in metric dimensions. Reviewer Sofia requested a short canary and explicit rollback steps in the runbook; reply: added runbook section and flag to disable checkpointing. Risk / mitigations: checkpoint store is ephemeral and GC'd to avoid disk growth. Trim is soft-shed and reversible; feature flag allows rollback. Circuit cooldown uses observed heartbeat windows to avoid global tune changes. Backcompat: none of the new fields change public API surfaces; CLI flag is ops-only. Merge: this PR was merged after approval; squash-and-merge with single commit message that consolidates commits and notes canary results and rollback steps.
